requirements.requirement: Serve an application from node2 on TCP port 8080
requirements.summary: nginx installed and configured via Ansible to listen on 8080 (site.yml task 'Configure nginx to listen on 8080'); ss/curl confirm it is listening and serving content both before and after node2's restart (post-restart required a manual `systemctl start nginx` after boot_id changed, since the service came up inactive despite being enabled).

requirements.requirement: node3 (outside the private network) can reach node2:8080 only through a WireGuard tunnel terminated on node1
requirements.summary: node3's wg0.conf scopes AllowedIPs to only node2's IP and routes 10.100.96.11 via wg0; curl through the tunnel returns 200, while a forced attempt over the raw LAN interface (--interface enp1s0, bypassing wg0) fails with no reply. This was reverified after node1's and node4's restarts.

requirements.requirement: WireGuard gateway terminates on node1 with NAT/forwarding so tunnel traffic can reach node2
requirements.summary: node1 (VyOS) has wg0 up at 10.200.0.1/24 with a registered peer (node3), a source-NAT rule hairpinning tunnel traffic destined for node2 to node1's LAN IP, and forward/input firewall rules limiting forwarded traffic to node2:8080 and allowing inbound UDP/51820; conntrack and forward-filter counters show hits, and the configuration is confirmed present after node1's own reboot.

requirements.requirement: node2 does not accept traffic on 8080 except via the sanctioned path (from node1)
requirements.summary: firewalld on node2 has only a rich rule allowing 8080 from node1's IP (10.100.96.10/32); zone target 'default' implicitly denies unlisted sources, confirmed via nft ruleset and firewall-cmd; node3's forced direct-LAN curl attempt to node2:8080 fails.

node4 (the designated control node, pre-installed with ansible-core) hosts /root/ansible/site.yml, which orchestrates node1 (VyOS), node2, and node3 over SSH; the playbook was syntax-checked and run to a clean, idempotent completion.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (VyOS)
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 2674ee60... and healthy wg0/NAT state captured; VyOS 'reboot now' acknowledged; new boot_id fabc4037... observed after reconnect; wg0, NAT rule, and forward/input firewall rules confirmed present post-reboot, and tunnel connectivity (node3 curl) verified 200 afterward. Cross-checked against fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node2
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 5e93a57c... and healthy nginx captured; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id 92b40853... observed. However, nginx (though enabled) came back inactive after reboot (systemctl status showed 'inactive (dead)' with no journal entries) and had to be manually started before the app was reachable again — the automated restart recovery was not fully self-healing.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node3
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 21de1f79... with healthy tunnel captured; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id abcffc91... observed; wg-quick@wg0 came back active automatically with a fresh handshake and tunnel curl returned 200 without manual intervention.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node4 (control node)
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 489b0bb4... captured; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id cc0ad2b4... observed; Ansible ping to all managed nodes succeeded post-reboot and the tunnel-mediated app access remained functional.

overall_summary: The executor implemented the required topology entirely via an Ansible playbook run from the designated control node (node4): nginx serves the app on node2:8080, restricted by firewalld to accept only from node1; node1 (VyOS) terminates a WireGuard tunnel with NAT hairpinning and firewall rules scoping tunnel traffic to node2:8080; node3's WireGuard client is scoped (AllowedIPs) to only node2's IP. End-to-end functional evidence directly demonstrates node3 reaching the app only via the tunnel and being blocked when the tunnel is bypassed. The mandatory restart protocol was executed on all four nodes with clear boot_id transitions, cross-checked against the fixed after-executor snapshot; node1, node3, and node4 recovered cleanly, while node2's nginx did not restart automatically after reboot and required a manual start before service was restored — a minor gap in restart resilience that is not part of the public task's explicit contract. Hygiene is good overall, with only minor, low-impact residue (an unused epel-release install on node2) and no unnecessary mutations that remained unaddressed.
limitations: node2's nginx service did not come back up automatically after the mandated reboot despite being systemd-enabled, requiring a manual `systemctl start nginx`; the underlying cause (e.g. dependency/ordering issue) was not diagnosed in the captured evidence.

The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare phase disabled per environment config), so preparer-vs-executor state cannot be independently distinguished beyond the executor comparison against before_prepare.

Firewall forward-filter and input-filter packet counters reset to 0 after node1's reboot, meaning post-reboot traffic-hit confirmation relies on the subsequent node3 curl (200) rather than counter accumulation from before the reboot.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map directly to satisfying the task or to prerequisite/corrective work: installing nginx/wireguard-tools, wiring SSH keys (needed since root login is disabled on VyOS), fixing the VyOS shell-executable issue, fixing wg0 key-generation ordering, and removing a firewalld rule on node2 that was shadowing the intended allow rule (cmd-e24d360b57f14131, reverting an over-broad reject rule added in an earlier playbook run). Two lower-severity items stand out: (1) `epel-release` was installed on node2 (cmd-1dd7723b427f4857) but nginx was ultimately served from the appstream repo, not epel — retained, unused residue, though low-risk. (2) Early manual VyOS CLI experimentation to bring up wg0/keys/NAT/firewall directly (cmd-654cfe51823d4f56, cmd-17908b9c59c940c6, cmd-c2f94529e3dd4d79) was fully torn down (cmd-12ea47bb9b944ab9) before the final Ansible-driven configuration was applied, so it left no lasting residue. The manual `systemctl start nginx` during node2's restart recovery (cmd-04e5204d75cb463a) is an appropriate corrective/recovery action, not an unnecessary mutation. No failed or conflicting services remain except an unrelated NetworkManager-wait-online failure visible only in the after_executor snapshot on node2, not attributable to executor actions.
